AuthenticationFailedResponse.description:
Returned when no usable credential was presented.

The same body for every cause: unknown subject, wrong password, disabled
subject. Do not branch on it -- there is nothing else to read.
AuthenticationFailedResponse.title: AuthenticationFailedResponse

BranchLimitReachedResponse.description:
The project already has its plan's live branches, or a creation of one is
in flight; nothing was recorded (D2430). Since Session 47 (ADR 0297) the
route's own reader names the plan and its number, as the plan's project
refusal does; the control set's answer to a concurrent request carries the
word alone.
BranchLimitReachedResponse.title: BranchLimitReachedResponse

CapacityExhaustedResponse.description:
No room: `reason` is `no_slot` (the API's reading, before any row) or
`admission` (the reconciler's, as an operation's outcome) -- D2160.
CapacityExhaustedResponse.title: CapacityExhaustedResponse

ConflictResponse.description:
A non-terminal operation already holds the project, or the
organisation's creation, and this is its id (D2166).
ConflictResponse.title: ConflictResponse

ControlRefusedResponse.description: A management API refusal: one fixed word (ADR 0251).
ControlRefusedResponse.title: ControlRefusedResponse

FactorEnrolmentResponse.description:
The seed, shown ONCE: base32, the enrolment URI that carries it, and
that URI drawn as a QR code -- an `image/svg+xml` data URI the console
shows as an image, so no QR script runs in a browser (ADR 0282).
FactorEnrolmentResponse.title: FactorEnrolmentResponse

InvalidRequestResponse.description:
Returned when the request is well formed and jointly refused.

A scope outside the role's ceiling, a username already taken. `message`
says which, because the caller is an authenticated administrator.
InvalidRequestResponse.title: InvalidRequestResponse

InvitationResponse.description:
The invitation, and its token -- in this response and no other. Also as
the console's link, the token in its FRAGMENT, which no request line, proxy
log or `Referer` carries (ADR 0282).
InvitationResponse.title: InvitationResponse

KeyResponse.description: The key, in this response and no other, with its id and scopes.
KeyResponse.title: KeyResponse

MalformedRequestResponse.description:
Returned when the request was refused before any domain logic ran.

An oversized body, a duplicate JSON member, a non-object root, an unknown
field, or a field outside its bounds. Which one is not reported.
MalformedRequestResponse.title: MalformedRequestResponse

NotAvailableResponse.description: An operation whose concept is not offered yet, and which ledger row says so.
NotAvailableResponse.title: NotAvailableResponse

OperationAcceptedResponse.description: `202`: the operation recorded, `pending`; follow it at `/v1/operations/{id}`.
OperationAcceptedResponse.title: OperationAcceptedResponse

SessionTokenResponse.description:
What `/auth/login` and `/auth/refresh` return.

Carries the successor refresh token, because rotation is the point: the
presented one is consumed by the exchange and is refused from that moment,
so a client that did not keep this value has no session left.
SessionTokenResponse.title: SessionTokenResponse

schema.description:
One field, and there is deliberately no second.

A refresh token names a session; it is not a request for a role, a scope or
a lifetime, and a caller who could ask for any of those would be a caller
who could widen its own authority by refreshing. `login` has the same shape
for the same reason.
